candidates.original_title: Quantification and ACD: Evidence from Real Time Sentence Processing
candidates.description: HKV's Experiment 1: ACD relative clauses modifying a quantified object NP (every) are easier to process than those modifying a definite object NP (the), with a critical interaction between verb type and determiner in the words immediately following the disambiguating verb
candidates.citation_sentence: In a recent attempt to find on-line evidence for the existence of Quantifier Raising (QR), Hackl, Koster-Hale & Varvoutis (HKV;2012) reported that antecedent-contained-deletion (ACD) relative clauses modifying an object noun phrase (NP) whose determiner is "every" (e.g., "every doctor... was", as in (1a)) were easier to process than those modifying a object NP whose determiner is "the" (e.g., "the doctor... was").
candidates.notes: Failed to find the critical verb type × determiner interaction in any of the four word regions (15-18) following the disambiguating verb. Main effects of verb type were replicated but the predicted interaction was not significant in either participants or items ANOVAs. The authors explicitly conclude that HKV's experiments should not be viewed as providing evidence for the ACD quantifier raising processing effect.

candidates.original_title: Quantification and ACD: Evidence from Real Time Sentence Processing
candidates.description: In Experiment 1, quantified object noun phrases headed by “every” were predicted to show a processing advantage over definite object noun phrases headed by “the” in antecedent-contained-deletion relative clauses, reflected in an interaction between determiner and verb type after the disambiguating verb.
candidates.citation_sentence: In a recent attempt to find on-line evidence for the existence of Quantifier Raising (QR), Hackl, Koster-Hale & Varvoutis (HKV;2012) reported that antecedent-containeddeletion (ACD) relative clauses modifying an object noun phrase (NP) whose determiner is "every" (e.g., "every doctor... was", as in (1a)) were easier to process than those modifying a object NP whose determiner is "the" (e.g., "the doctor... was").
candidates.notes: Attempted direct replication of HKV Experiment 1 using self-paced reading. The replication authors explicitly conclude that they failed to find the predicted interaction.

candidates.description: In Experiment 2, the critical prediction was that the definite determiner condition would be read more slowly than the quantified condition specifically in local antecedent-contained-deletion clauses, producing an interaction between verb type and determiner after the disambiguating verb.
